business_problem: EvenUp needed to turn huge, inconsistent personal-injury case files into accurate demands, summaries, and discovery documents fast enough for smaller firms to compete, without letting polished but incorrect reasoning slip through.
solution_summary: EvenUp built AI Drafts on the Claude Platform as a multi-stage document pipeline for personal-injury work. Case files often exceed 1,000 pages and include medical records, billing ledgers, police reports, scanned bills, and checkbox forms. The system climbs a cost ladder: it reads native text first, uses standard OCR where possible, and escalates to Claude vision only for the pages other methods cannot handle. Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku manage routine extraction, while Claude Opus 4.8 handles the deeper reasoning needed to keep a thirty-page demand internally consistent and legally persuasive. EvenUp layers PI-specific data, routing, verification, and automated workflows on top, so facts get normalized once and then reused across demands, negotiation sheets, and discovery responses. Internally, teams also use Claude Enterprise and Claude Code for forecasting and debugging-agent projects.

data_flow: Medical records, billing ledgers, police reports, and scanned forms enter AI Drafts; the pipeline reads native text first, then OCR, then Claude vision when needed, and routes the extracted facts into Claude reasoning layers that assemble demands, negotiation sheets, and discovery documents with reusable structured evidence.
business_outcome: EvenUp reduced drafting from eight to fifteen hours of skilled legal work per case to finished drafts in about 30 minutes, raised settlement offers by 300 percent, helped customer firms clear backlogs and triple demand output, and improved smaller-case expense accuracy and overall draft completeness.
